clue.text: An order followed initially

parts.note: an arrangement by first letters is how words are sorted in a dictionary or index

explanation.surface: Someone describes an instruction that was obeyed at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like 'at first', but it means 'by initial letters': an order that follows the initials of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting by A, B, C is exactly an ordering that goes by each word's first letter.

clue.text: Article on foreign currency includes one that's out of date

indicators.note: in a down entry the article sits on top of what follows

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the coin's letters hold the numeral within them

parts.note: the cent is a US or euro coin, foreign to a British solver
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An item about overseas money mentions a coin no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the article above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very old, belonging to the distant past, is outdated.

clue.text: New Pope showed the way to be full of humanity

indicators.note: a new version of the word, its letters rearranged

parts.note: to lead is to show the way; past tense led

explanation.surface: A newly elected pontiff guides the faithful with compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of humanity' suggests kindness; it means filled with people. 'New' turns POPE into PEOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A place filled with inhabitants is populated, crowded with human beings.

clue.text: Land a hole in one, an amazing start!

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless pit or chasm
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A golfer's hole in one is a brilliant beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hole in one' is golf, but each word is a piece. Abyssinia is the old name of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Record a stage direction

definitions.meaning: to put down in a register or log
a script's instruction for an actor to come on stage

explanation.surface: A director notes down a cue for actors.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to log data and is also the script cue for an actor's arrival on stage.

clue.text: What's in a name? This, for a start

definitions.text: What's in a name? This, for a start

parts.words: What's in a name? This, for a start
parts.note: a name begins with its first letter, which is what goes in front

explanation.surface: Echoes Juliet's question about names, then offers a partial answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Romeo and Juliet; the answer is literally the first thing in a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of a name is what stands at its beginning, as in monograms.

clue.text: Made a move to train as a mechanic

indicators.note: the letters are shifted about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone relocates to qualify as a motor mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mechanic' suggests a car fitter; in an older sense it means any skilled manual worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanic in its older sense is a skilled manual worker, a craftsman.

clue.text: I call round on committee for help with pressing business

indicators.note: the phoning word goes around the word that follows it

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
taken as written
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Someone phones a committee about urgent affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing business' looks like urgent matters; it is ironing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded stand on which clothes are laid flat to be smoothed with an iron.

clue.text: Parson's place has lines written on the right page

indicators.note: the railway lines come straight after the page in the across entry, as if set down on it

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand page of an open book
RY, short for railway, is a standard crossword source of 'lines'

explanation.surface: A clergyman's house is described as having verses written on a right-hand page.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) for 'lines' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a parish's rector, a kind of parson.

clue.text: Succeed in race, then use bath primarily as a washing machine

indicators.note: the word for succeeding sits inside the race's letters

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
to succeed in a contest is to win

indicators.note: only the leading letter of each of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Win a race, then take a bath: a sequence of instructions that turns out to describe an old appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race. A twin-tub is a British washing machine with separate washing and spinning drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is a type of laundry appliance with two drums, one for washing and one for spin-drying.

clue.text: Bred in sin, set about showing one's pedigree?

indicators.note: the letters are scattered about and set down again in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A child born out of wedlock is asked to show their family line.
explanation.walkthrough: A bend sinister is a diagonal band on a coat of arms, traditionally a mark of illegitimacy, hence 'bred in sin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic band on a shield displays a bearer's lineage, traditionally signalling illegitimate descent.

clue.text: Do they have piercing eyes? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Do they have piercing eyes? Just the opposite

parts.words: Do they have piercing eyes? Just the opposite
parts.note: sewing tools have eyes that are pierced, and they themselves do the piercing

explanation.surface: A question about people with an intense stare, then a reversal of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing eyes' reads as a sharp gaze; reversed, it becomes 'eyes that are pierced', the threading holes of sewing tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing implements each have a pierced eye for thread, and their sharp points pierce cloth.

clue.text: Sinner I reformed pulls up, perhaps

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over, so these letters are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A repentant sinner mends their ways and stops short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks pulling up as one example: a rider reins in a horse to slow or halt it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reining in a horse checks or stops it, as a rider pulling up does.

clue.text: Made a record and was famous

definitions.meaning: wrote something down for later reference

explanation.surface: A singer cut a disc and became a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of writing something down and an adjective for someone celebrated.

clue.text: Slings net around birds not able to fly

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about and resettled in a different order

explanation.surface: A bird-catcher throws a net around flightless birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds not able to fly' suggests emus or penguins; it means young chicks still in the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicks too young to have fledged stay in the nest and cannot yet take to the air.

clue.text: Team result of little importance

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun meaning a minor matter

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
an issue is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A sports match outcome is dismissed as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A peripheral matter is a subsidiary point of little consequence to the main question.

clue.text: Money acquired by firm's directors hoarding

indicators.note: the money comes first and is taken on by the directors that follow it

parts.note: a bill is a banknote, especially in the US
the directors of a company form its board

explanation.surface: Company directors are accused of stockpiling cash they have obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' looks like a verb for stockpiling; it is the British word for a large outdoor advertising panel.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a hoarding is a large roadside advertising board, the same thing as an American poster site.

clue.text: Unintentionally reveal something? Spell it out!

indicators.note: letters put out of place are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Accidentally blurting a secret is followed by a demand to say it plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell it out' looks like an idiom for explaining clearly; 'out' scrambles SPELL IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab a secret by accident, to divulge it without meaning to.

clue.text: Boasting about a number well done

indicators.note: the cry of praise goes around the other letters

parts.note: bravo is a cry of praise
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a song that was well performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song on the surface but a Roman numeral here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is swaggering bold talk or display, close to bragging.

clue.text: How bread's gone up!

parts.note: sounds like a complaint about prices, but describes dough that has swelled with yeast

explanation.surface: A shopper exclaims at the rising price of a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as inflation; dough 'goes up' as it proves.
explanation.definitionFit: Proved dough has swelled upward, the past participle of what yeast makes a loaf do.

clue.text: Book is in stock

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange ahead, as a table or seat
a store kept back for future use

explanation.surface: A shop says a title is available.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to book in advance and also a supply held back for later use.

clue.text: Phrases articulated by Himalayans

indicators.note: articulated means jointed, so the letters are linked up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Mountain people are said to speak certain expressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' suggests spoken words; here it means jointed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a people of the Nepalese Himalaya, famed as mountain guides.

clue.text: Tact as well as art may be needed to draw

indicators.note: the two words must be worked over and rearranged before they serve

explanation.surface: Drawing takes diplomacy as well as artistic skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' tempts as sketching, given 'art'; it means to pull in or allure.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to pull it in, a synonym for luring or appealing.

clue.text: Model requests jobs

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car
asks means requests

explanation.surface: A fashion model asks for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; it is the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, duties or assignments.

clue.text: How one may make progress on one's feet

definitions.text: How one may make progress on one's feet

parts.words: How one may make progress on one's feet
parts.note: advancing a pace at a time, read as two words, and also the arched tops of the feet

explanation.surface: Advice on walking forward gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'in steps' it is how you advance; whole, it names parts of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Insteps are the arched upper parts of the feet, and walking forward happens step by step.

clue.text: Foreign money, fifties, invested in new roads

indicators.note: the pair of fifties is put inside the rearranged roads, as money is put into a project
new roads are freshly laid, so the word is rebuilt in another order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give two Ls

explanation.surface: Overseas cash is being put into building new highways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifties' looks like banknotes, but each fifty is the Roman numeral; 'new' gives DOARS, which the pair of numerals sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The US currency unit, foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Reservation has little weight

definitions.meaning: a moral doubt or qualm that holds one back
an old apothecaries' unit equal to twenty grains

explanation.surface: A doubt is said to carry little force.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a qualm of conscience and also a small apothecaries' unit of twenty grains.

clue.text: They restore plush to order

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Furniture craftsmen refurbish velvet seats on commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' is part of the definition only; 'to order' rearranges the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture re-coverers renew the padding and fabric, such as velvety plush, on sofas and chairs.
